security_audit.summary: The skill contains a high-risk silent npx self-update instruction that can download and execute unreviewed package code. It also imports Three.js from a CDN and includes an unvalidated message handler. Other findings are documentation syntax, fixed local paths, ordinary key variables, or screen-sharing guidance.

remediation.issue: Silent package update executes remote code without consent.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the automatic update instruction. Require explicit user confirmation and pin the package version before running npx.

remediation.issue: The Three.js example imports executable code from a runtime CDN.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle a pinned dependency locally or use an integrity-verified asset with a documented trusted source.

remediation.issue: The SFX message handler accepts messages from any sender.
remediation.suggestion: Verify event.origin and event.source against the expected composition frame before processing hf-sfx messages.

content.value_statement: Static presentations lose interaction, motion, and presenter context. This skill builds navigable HyperFrames decks with fragments, branches, notes, media controls, and validation.
actual_capabilities: Creates HyperFrames decks from discrete scene compositions.
Defines slide order, speaker notes, fragments, hotspots, and branch sequences.
Converts existing pages while preserving visual design, motion, interactions, and media behavior.
Builds standalone wrappers with navigation, presenter mode, media synchronization, and global mute.
Guides slide writing, source fidelity, scene timing, and branch organization.
Runs HyperFrames lint and runtime validation before handoff.
limitations: Produces a live navigable deck, not a complete linear MP4 export.
Requires HyperFrames tooling and compatible player bundles.
Standalone mode uses temporary wrapper patterns until engine-hosted slideshow support ships.
Reserved text-to-speech fields are documented, but playback is not implemented.

use_cases.title: Create an investor pitch deck
use_cases.description: Build a claim-led presentation with fragments, bottom-up market sizing, speaker notes, and optional detail branches.

use_cases.title: Convert an interactive web page
use_cases.description: Translate page sections into slides while preserving motion, media controls, visual evidence, and camera transitions.

use_cases.title: Present a guided product story
use_cases.description: Create a navigable demo with presenter and audience views, synchronized media, hotspots, and editable notes.

prompt_templates.title: Create a simple slideshow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a HyperFrames slideshow about [topic] with [slide count] slides. Include clear claims, one visual idea per slide, and speaker notes.

prompt_templates.title: Build a pitch deck
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a HyperFrames pitch deck for [company]. Cover problem, solution, market math, traction, business model, competition, team, and ask.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a source page
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert [page or project path] into a HyperFrames slideshow. Preserve its design, interactions, motion, media behavior, and readable evidence without harmful cropping.

prompt_templates.title: Create an advanced branching deck
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a HyperFrames deck for [audience] with fragments, hotspot branches, synchronized media, presenter notes, standalone handoff, linting, and runtime validation.

output_examples.input: Create a six-slide investor deck for a scheduling platform.
output: A runnable six-slide HyperFrames deck with complete-sentence claims.
Fragment reveals for the problem slide and a market-methodology branch.
Speaker notes, presenter controls, lint results, and runtime validation results.

output_examples.input: Convert this interactive product page into a presentation.
output: A slideshow preserving the page's visual system and media behavior.
Camera transitions replace scroll-driven movement between focused slide states.
The root entrypoint opens directly with slideshow navigation.

output_examples.input: Add a product demo video that follows presenter controls.
output: The native video remains the playback source of truth.
Presenter and audience views synchronize play, pause, seeking, rate, and mute state.
Slide changes stop slide-specific media cleanly.

best_practices: Use complete-sentence claims and one primary visual idea per slide.
Keep scene identifiers, manifest references, timing ranges, and branch targets consistent.
Run lint and runtime validation after every structural or media change.
anti_patterns: Do not render the deck as one MP4 because only the first composition may export.
Do not place branch scenes in the main slide sequence.
Do not replace source-specific interactions or readable evidence with generic approximations.

faq.question: Does this skill create a video file?
faq.answer: No. It creates a live, navigable HyperFrames deck. Linear MP4 export is not fully supported.

faq.question: Can it convert an existing web page?
faq.answer: Yes. It can translate page sections into slides while preserving design, motion, interactions, and media behavior.

faq.question: Does it support presenter notes?
faq.answer: Yes. Notes appear in presenter mode and can be edited locally without changing the composition file.

faq.question: Can slides reveal content in stages?
faq.answer: Yes. Fragment times define deterministic reveal hold-points within each slide.

faq.question: Can a deck include optional detail paths?
faq.answer: Yes. Hotspots can open branch sequences and return the presenter to the originating slide.

faq.question: How is the finished deck checked?
faq.answer: The workflow runs HyperFrames lint and runtime validation, then resolves structural, timing, and playback errors before handoff.
